description: Persist completed Rewrite operations (plan ID, files affected, timestamp, success/failure) in a local SQLite store so operators can audit what the scenario actually changed. Read-only API on the audit trail; no replay capability in v1.

requirements.description: Persist all completed Rewrite operations in a local SQLite store. Each persisted record must include: plan_id, list of affected files, operation types applied, timestamp of apply, and success/failure status with error message on failure. Expose a read-only API (RewriteHistory RPC) for querying the audit trail. No replay capability in v1: the API is read-only. The SQLite store must be initialized automatically on server start with the required schema.
requirements.title: Rewrite Operation Log Persistence in SQLite

validation.notes: Test that a successful Rewrite apply persists a record with correct plan_id, affected files, timestamp, and success status
Test that a failed Rewrite apply persists a record with failure status and error message
Test SQLite schema initialization creates the required table with all required columns
Test RewriteHistory query returns records in reverse-chronological order
Test that replay/mutation operations on persisted records are rejected (read-only enforcement)
End-to-end: run Rewrite apply, then call RewriteHistory RPC, verify the completed operation appears in the response
Server restart test: persisted records survive server restart and are accessible via RewriteHistory RPC after restart
Concurrent Rewrite applies persist separate records without data corruption
Operators can audit all filesystem changes made by the scenario without inspecting server logs
RewriteHistory RPC is accessible via CLI and UI as with all other capabilities

title: Operation Log Persistence
